/projects/thinknube-ai.title: Alejandro Arab's Project Thinknube.AI
p: ThinkNube is an AI-powered market research SaaS platform developed by Nube Research. The platform allows companies to create conversational research studies using an AI agent that interviews participants through channels such as WhatsApp, Instagram, or direct links. The product automates processes that traditionally require research agencies, manual interviews, and long analysis cycles. Teams can design studies, reach participants, and analyze insights within a single platform.

Companies often rely on expensive research agencies or data-only tools that lack real interaction with consumers. ThinkNube addresses this by combining artificial intelligence with real consumer interviews.

The approach focused on balancing AI automation with a clear and intuitive user experience. Product flows were designed for study creation, audience segmentation, and insights analysis. I worked on product architecture, study creation flows, dashboard design, and the overall visual direction of the platform.

The vision was to democratize access to market research, enabling companies of any size to gather real user insights quickly without relying on traditional agencies. The design focused on clarity, professionalism, and trust while maintaining the simplicity of a modern SaaS platform.

A key challenge was structuring complex research parameters such as segmentation, quotas, and response validation into a simple configuration flow. The platform needed to manage multiple variables within a single experience without overwhelming users.

Users can define objectives, select audiences, configure parameters, and monitor responses in real time. Quality control tools help detect unreliable answers. The system also includes response quality monitoring and analytics dashboards.

The result was a solid MVP of an AI-powered research platform capable of automating interviews and generating structured insights. The product combines automation with a human-centered approach, using AI to facilitate research while preserving real consumer feedback.

/projects/brikka.title: Alejandro Arab's Project Brikka
p: Brikka is a blockchain-based platform that enables tokenization of real estate projects. It connects developers seeking funding with investors who want to participate through digital assets. Users can invest in different components of a construction project represented as tokens, allowing participation with different levels of capital.

Traditional real estate investments require high capital and intermediary processes. At the same time, many developments require financing to move forward. Brikka addresses this by enabling projects to raise capital through tokenization, making investments accessible to a wider range of investors.

The full product experience was designed including the landing page, investor platform, and project management dashboard. The goal was to structure complex processes — token creation, investment simulation, and wallet management — into an intuitive and understandable experience.

The goal was to democratize real estate investing by allowing participation with smaller capital through tokenization. The design focused on communicating security, transparency, and control over investments.

A major challenge was integrating decentralized wallets and multiple token types into clear investment flows. The system needed to manage multiple token types associated with different parts of each real estate project while supporting investment flows connected to decentralized wallets.

Users can explore projects, simulate returns, connect their wallet, and invest directly within the platform. An administrative dashboard allows developers to upload projects, configure tokens, and manage investment parameters.

A functional MVP of a real estate tokenization platform was delivered and prepared for validation. Although the client decided to pause the project due to changes in the economic environment, the product remained ready for further validation and potential launch.

/projects/fan-raise.title: Alejandro Arab's Project Fan Raise
/projects/fan-raise.description: Web & Mobile App for Sports-Based Fundraising
p: FanRaise is a web and mobile platform that enables nonprofit organizations to raise funds through sports engagement. Fans participate by making pledge-based donations tied to predictions about sports events. If the prediction is correct, the user fulfills their pledge and can participate in prize draws or rewards. The platform connects organizations, athletes, teams, and fans in an experience that blends sports entertainment with social impact.

Nonprofit organizations often struggle to maintain long-term donor engagement. Traditional fundraising campaigns rely on direct donations that can feel passive to younger audiences. FanRaise addresses this by turning donations into an interactive experience tied to sports events.

I led the full product design process from early strategic discussions to high-fidelity prototypes. The goal was to create a simple experience that combines sports predictions, donations, and gamification. I also designed the visual identity and logo of the product, aligning the brand with the emotional and participatory tone of the experience. Flows were designed both for fans participating in events and for organizations creating fundraising campaigns.

The vision was to transform how fans support social causes by leveraging the excitement of sports. Instead of passive donations, users actively participate by predicting sports outcomes. This creates a more engaging and emotional fundraising experience that connects entertainment with social impact.

One of the main challenges was designing a system that combines multiple mechanics: sports predictions, pledge donations, rewards, and event management. The interface needed to keep the experience simple while supporting these complex interactions.

Users can explore sports events, select a prediction, and choose a pledge donation amount. If the prediction is correct, the pledged donation is completed. Organizations and teams can create events, define participation rules, and monitor results through dedicated dashboards.

The result was a fully designed web and mobile platform for sports-based fundraising. Product flows include event discovery, predictions, donations, and campaign management. The project demonstrates how sports engagement can create new forms of social participation and fundraising.

/about.title: Alejandro Arab's About
/about.description: Get to know me a little better.
h1: Get to know me a little better
p: I'm Ale, a Product Designer who over the last 6 years has worked across a wide range of industries and product types. I work close to the team and close to the problem, from early decisions to final handoff. I like being in the room where things get decided, asking questions before it's too late, and staying involved until the end. I also teach design and prototyping on the side, which keeps me honest about what actually matters and what is just habit.

Collaboration is where most of the real work happens for me. I spend a lot of time with developers, PMs, and clients, not just handing off files but figuring things out together. Whether I'm building a design system, mapping out a complex flow, or going back and forth on a single interaction, I try to stay close to the craft at every scale. The details are part of the job, not a bonus round at the end.

Outside the screen, I cook, play bass and synthesizers, and travel with my partner Pía whenever we get the chance. We're both designers, so wherever we end up we're usually working, sketching, or collecting references without really meaning to. I'm also a big video game fan and my Nintendo Switch comes on every trip. At home we share the space with our two cats, Roma and Venus, who have pretty firm opinions about our work hours and who gets to use the office chairs. I grew up with a background in gastronomy before landing in design, and I think that attention to ingredients, timing, process, mise en place, and how something finally comes together is simply part of how I design today.
